title: Pulled-back injective modules are acyclic for object sections
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites in the common universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1), with associated geometric morphism $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism] and $g^{-1}M=M\circ u$. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal D$, put $R'=g^{-1}R$, and let $I$ be an injective $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ let $E_U$ be the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the free $R'$-module presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}R'(V)$, with restriction sending the basis vector of $a$ to that of its composite with the restriction arrow. Then for every integer $p>0$ one has $\operatorname{Ext}_{R'}^p(E_U,g^{-1}I)=0$. Here $\operatorname{Ext}_{R'}^p(E_U,F)=H^p\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(E_U,J^\bullet)$ for an injective resolution $F\to J^\bullet$, and it is the right derived functor of $F\mapsto F(U)$ under the natural identification $\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(E_U,F)=F(U)$.

from.place: Proof (1)--(2), semistable-alteration input in the nearby-cycle branch: ILO Exposé X, Theorem 3.4, Step 3, invoking Temkin 2010, Theorems 1.5 and 1.1 for a semistable multipointed modification. Temkin proof component: Marked dualizing line bundle and contracted-component degrees. Auxiliary input: Local complete-intersection determinant adjunction underlying the marked dualizing construction, before the marking is inserted. Supporting ring/sheaf input: Transitivity triangle for ring cotangent complexes. Proof of the supporting transitivity triangle: polynomial differential sequence, derived category homology comparisons, and identification of functoriality maps. Generic homological input to the category bar resolution: Unbounded derived lower shriek for continuous and cocontinuous site functors. Supporting input: The higher Ext vanishing for each free module generator against the inverse image of an injective, used in the bounded-above acyclicity test.
